name: Physical AI — Train a Robot in Simulation and Watch It Learn

why_simulate.hook: We train robots in a simulator before the real world. Why not just use the real robot?
why_simulate.recall: Why train robots in simulation first?
why_simulate.answer: safe, fast, cheap, massively parallel — thousands of tries with no broken hardware

digital_twin.hook: The robot in sim has to behave like the real one. What's that virtual copy called?
digital_twin.answer: a physics-accurate virtual copy of the robot + environment to train and test in

isaac_stack.hook: NVIDIA gives you the GPU simulator AND the RL framework. What are they?
isaac_stack.recall: What are Isaac Sim / Isaac Lab for?
isaac_stack.answer: a GPU physics simulator + an RL framework to train robot control policies

rl_loop.hook: A robot learns to move with NO one telling it the right moves. How?
rl_loop.recall: The RL loop — agent, environment, reward, episode?
rl_loop.answer: agent acts -> environment returns new state + reward -> agent updates to earn more reward, over episodes

agent_env.hook: Two halves of every RL setup. Which decides, which judges?
agent_env.answer: agent = the policy choosing actions; environment = the world returning state + reward

obs_action.hook: The policy needs to SEE something and DO something. What are those two called?
obs_action.answer: observation = what the policy senses; action = what it can control (joint torques, etc.)

reward_shaping.hook: The thing that makes or breaks a policy isn't the algorithm. What is it?
reward_shaping.recall: Why is reward design the craft of RL?
reward_shaping.answer: the policy optimizes exactly what you reward — a bad reward gets gamed / wrong behavior

ppo_training.hook: You hit train and watch the curves. What algorithm, and what proves it's learning?
ppo_training.recall: What does PPO do, and what shows learning?
ppo_training.answer: PPO improves the policy from collected experience; a rising reward curve = it's learning

reality_gap.hook: Perfect in sim, clumsy in reality. What's that gap — and the fix?
reality_gap.answer: sim != real differences; randomize sim physics/visuals so the policy generalizes to the real world

teleoperation.hook: Step inside the simulator and drive the robot yourself. Why would you?
teleoperation.recall: What is teleoperation / VR embodiment in robotics?
teleoperation.answer: a human drives/demonstrates the robot (e.g. from a Quest) — for control + collecting demo data

policy_deploy.hook: Training's done. How do you actually USE the trained policy?
policy_deploy.recall: How do you run a trained policy after training?
policy_deploy.answer: export it (e.g. ONNX) and run it to control the robot in sim or reality
